evidence: task/environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template Dockerfile (both sha256 0a75419e9598ded9317b26bbf0d2b12de0b9b11185fb4c9fed1ca7f3e52467d1). Every item of the skill's row-15 verify list holds: base `FROM node:22-bookworm-slim` (line 1, template base, no --platform); `ENV NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules` (line 3); runtime deps pre-installed at build with exact pins `npm install -g ... express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1` (lines 9-12); `COPY instructions/ /instructions/` and `COPY assets/ /assets/` (lines 14-15); `chmod -R a+rX /instructions /assets` and `/app` created, git-initialised with only .gitkeep committed (lines 16-23). No COPY/ADD of solution/ or tests/. task.toml sets no [environment].docker_image, so the Dockerfile is actually built. The golden's full non-builtin require graph is exactly express (src/index.js:18) and better-sqlite3 (src/db.js:7), matching package.json pins 5.1.0/12.4.1; all other requires are Node built-ins. solve.sh performs no install. Public contract agrees: instruction.md:13 'Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages'; integration.md:3-4 'Express and better-sqlite3 already available through NODE_PATH'. Seed asset /assets/seed_data.json parses and equals the golden's copy. Verifier image (tests/Dockerfile) uses the same node:22-bookworm-slim runtime and installs the same express@5.1.0/better-sqlite3@12.4.1 pins, so a native-module ABI mismatch between phases is not expected. Counterexample attempts: (a) a weak app requiring an extra npm package (e.g. ws) would crash in both images, so the image does not hide a dependency; it is correctly excluded by the public 'don't install packages' rule; (b) a conforming app using only Express/better-sqlite3/built-ins via NODE_PATH and copying seed data from world-readable /assets into /app is fully supported, so no conforming alternative fails because of the image. Notes (not defects, template-controlled): base image is tag-pinned not digest-pinned and apt packages are unpinned (workbook: unpinned apt is a NOTE). No agent-image docker build was recorded in this round's raw evidence index; the verdict rests on static byte-identity with the template and the exact-pinned install lines, and the golden run used the verifier image (hireops-verifier:20261002-permission-repair) with the same pins.
